cells.tense: Right now, with your hand on the pen, the harvest is being tallied and shared.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: Let your own read on fairness settle a small case between you and someone near — no polling it, no announcing it. Then close it. What you owe gets paid and the matter is done with.
cells.core:
You can read what you owe in a relationship without running a ledger. That is the harvest at your feet — not a tally, a clear sense of what's fair, both directions moving while it holds. Not many can do that without turning it into a scale. You do, and whoever is next to you can feel it.

There's a loose end threaded through one of your connections. Let your sense of fairness settle it the way it wants to — no second opinion, no announcement. Then leave it alone. What should have been given gets given and the account closes.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair without anyone doing the math.
cells.place: Among the people, where feeling-with runs close to the skin

cells.tense: Soon the exchange will be weighed before it has happened, each debt tallied in advance.
cells.act: spend an hour with the thing you love without a task attached to it
cells.ask: Spend an hour with one person you love and attach nothing to it. Don't read them, don't settle anything, don't sift it afterward. Just the hour. When it ends, it ends.
cells.core:
In how you connect, what passes between you and another person is being watched closely now, each move weighed before it lands. You can feel what's fair almost before it happens, and that quickness keeps things even. It also means nothing gets to rest. Your attention sits on the scale while someone is still with you.

What's underneath does not need the accounting to be real. Sit with one person you love for an hour and do nothing with it. If the tally fades after a few tries, that's what you get. If it doesn't, you've lost nothing. Under the watching there is a plain knowing of how things stand, and it can be felt without becoming a verdict.
cells.sheetLine: You're summing up what isn't due yet.
cells.place: Among the people, where feeling-with runs close to the skin

cells.tense: You are at the door still, the exchange already behind you when it was made.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Reach one person you've been meaning to reach, at a speed you could keep long-term — a note you'd send a second time, a walk you'd repeat. Not one brave day. One reach, steady, then stop there.
cells.core:
With people you have been holding back — contact kept thin enough not to ask anything of you, reaching out in ways that don't have to land, or not reaching at all. The feeling is real, and the small reach you make is real too. But it moves at a speed you can't keep, so it keeps stopping short. What landed, landed. What didn't, you are still beside.

The people you wish you were closer to don't need one perfect arrival. Pick one and go toward them at a pace you could keep going — a short note you'd send again, a walk you'd take again. Stay steady. The doing and the caring travel the same road when you let them walk.
cells.sheetLine: You reach in bursts, then stop, while the feeling stays.

cells.tense: Now you are setting the order of things outward and saying it was always just how it was.
cells.act: state the order of things once, without argument
cells.ask: Say once, to whoever it involves, what an arrangement between you two actually is — its shape, its terms, in plain words. Say it one time. No case for it and no softening after.
cells.core:
You've been reading the room — what a connection needs, where the lines sit, how to hold a space steady — and doing it so smoothly it looks like following. That reading is yours, and it's good. What's missing is 'I made it.' You put it down to circumstance, and it isn't circumstance. The shape holds around the two of you, and only you don't say so.

Saying it does not require arguing for it. Say once, to whoever it involves, what the arrangement between you actually is — its shape and its terms, in plain words. Flat and straight, one time. That is already yours to say.
cells.sheetLine: The reading is yours. You keep filing it under luck.
cells.place: Among the people, where feeling-with runs close to the skin
